_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. The mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so the (non-)oracle registration and the catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `s.writer.writer` is a semio-NATIVE artifact — it is persisted as `.dsl.semio` text and `.pack.semio` binary through this subset's own codecs, and no third party reads or writes either — so no oracle is registered; see noOracleDecisions below.

oracles.rationale:
A second implementation of the `s.writer.writer` document and its four typed mutations, in Python, at `../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-writer-1/🐍️component.py`. Written from `../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🔣️.json` (the five members), rule 1 of `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️12/SEMANTIC-MUTATIONS-OVERHAUL/📓️derivation-rules.md`, and the four committed `(before, mutation, after, outcome)` vectors. It imports nothing from this repository and transliterates none of its Rust. This registration SUPERSEDES the `writer-document-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision, whose argument was refuted in this same wave by the fifteen `📕️norm` and nineteen `🧿️semio` references, all of which took Python second implementations over this same carrier. A THIRD-PARTY library was declined, not merely absent: nothing outside this repository models an editor document whose body is a CHILD ARTIFACT addressed by content rather than held inline, and none of them reads this carrier. WHAT THIS CASE'S EVIDENCE ACTUALLY COVERS, stated rather than implied: three of the four kinds are document-level scalar setters and are fully adjudicated, with the reference additionally asserting in role that each writes exactly ONE of the five members and never the composed child handle. THREE OF THE NINE SCENARIOS ARE REFUSED BY CLAUSE. `edit-text` in both roles: it writes the document's BODY, which this snapshot does not carry — it carries a composed child handle into an `s.stdio.semio@v1/document` — and the committed vector pins a `mutation.no-op` meaning the verb decided the new text was IDENTICAL to what the child already held, while neither the child's content nor the comparison rule is stated anywhere a second implementation can read; nor is the other branch, since no committed vector shows what the handle becomes when the text really changes. Adding one vector that carries the child body — the `scene` array `mutate-playbook-1` and `mutate-forms-1` already put in their own doc strings — plus the child-addressing rule, closes it. And `identity-round-trip`: the committed grammar `../🧬️schema/../🚪️io/📸️snapshot/📝️text/📖️.grammar.semio` is the repository-wide placeholder `payload = OCTET+` whose header production declares `"schema" SP "stdio.json"`, contradicted by the artifact's own first line `semio writer.writer.dsl v1`; the artifact's body is four HEX-ENCODED scalars and a `[hex,hex]` child-handle pair, and no committed document says the values are hex, that the pair is `(childId, target)`, or how the second element's `<artifactId>!<kind>@<standard>/<subset>` spelling is split. `package` is deliberately empty: the implementation needs no distribution, so this entry contributes nothing to `🔒️dependencies.json`.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `writer-1-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 4-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.
